previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: James, a 60-year-old man with severe COPD, chronic alcohol use disorder, and a history of frequent hospitalizations, was admitted to the MICU with respiratory distress and severe alcohol intoxication. He was hypoxemic on arrival, with a low oxygen saturation of 82% on room air, and required supplemental oxygen and bronchodilator treatments. Imaging revealed bibasilar atelectasis and chronic emphysema, but no pulmonary embolism or acute intracranial process. He experienced significant agitation during withdrawal, requiring sedation with Haldol and lorazepam, as well as temporary physical restraints for safety. Due to his repeated elopements, non-adherence to treatment, and inability to care for himself, a Section 35 petition was pursued. After stabilization of his respiratory status and withdrawal symptoms, he was discharged to police custody for involuntary substance use treatment. His oxygen levels stabilized in the low 90s, appropriate for his COPD, and he completed a course of steroids and antibiotics.

Brief Hospital Course:
Patient admitted to the hospital for COPD exacerbation and 
alcohol intoxication.

On the floor overnight he was started on a CIWA scale to monitor 
for withdrawal symptoms.  He was also treated for a COPD flare 
with steroids & azithromycin.  

On the morning after his hospitalization he expressed the desire 
to leave against medical advice because he wanted intravenous 
pain medications.  It was explained to him that he has a serious 
medical condition that requires treatment in the hospital.  He 
was informed of the risks and expressed his understanding.  
Several moments later he decided to stay in the hospital because 
he felt too short of breath.  Treatment continued at that time.  
However, later in the morning he was found missing from his 
room, consistent with elopement from the hospital without 
warning.  Despite attempts to locate him, he could not be found.
